reason: S1 changes wuffs_base__status from int32_t to a struct containing code and changes status-string APIs to accept int32_t. H0 still treats statuses as scalars and passes whole status structs to string functions, so both fuzz targets are incompatible with S1 and cannot exercise their decoding attack surfaces.
evidence: S1 declares `typedef struct { int32_t code; } wuffs_base__status`.
gif_fuzzer.c uses `if (z)`, compares `z == WUFFS_BASE__SUSPENSION_END_OF_DATA`, assigns `z = WUFFS_BASE__STATUS_OK`, and calls `wuffs_gif__status__string(z)`, all using the obsolete scalar protocol.
zlib_fuzzer.c uses `if (z)`, compares `z != WUFFS_BASE__SUSPENSION_SHORT_WRITE`, and calls `wuffs_zlib__status__string(z)`, likewise using the obsolete scalar protocol.
recommended_action: Update both harnesses to inspect `z.code` or use `wuffs_base__status__is_ok`, `wuffs_base__status__is_error`, and `wuffs_base__status__is_suspension`; pass `z.code` to package status-string functions and construct assigned statuses with `WUFFS_BASE__MAKE_STATUS`. Then build and fuzz both GIF and zlib targets.
